name: Mary
overview: Mary is a female biblical figure known primarily as the sister of Martha, as explicitly stated in Luke 10:39. While her tribe and additional personal details are not recorded, her familial connection highlights her role within the New Testament narrative. There are no additional notes provided about her beyond this relationship.
namesAndTitles: The name Mary carries several possible meanings, including 'bitterness,' 'plump one,' 'wished-for child,' and 'one who loves or is loved,' reflecting the richness of the Hebrew or Greek origins. This variety of meanings suggests the depth and commonality of the name in Scripture, as noted in Luke 10:39.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Mary as the sister of Martha (Luke 10:39) and, by inference, the sister of Lazarus (John 11:1). These relationships place her within a close-knit family known for their interactions with Jesus during His ministry.
scriptureSignificance: Mary's significance in the biblical narrative stems from her close association with Jesus and her family, who were notable figures during His earthly ministry. Her presence alongside Martha and Lazarus provides insight into the personal relationships Jesus maintained. Though not detailed here, her role exemplifies faithful discipleship and hospitality, contributing to the broader understanding of Jesus' ministry and the community that surrounded Him.
